PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-09-17
36F, outpatient visit for a routine evaluation.

S:
Patient presents for a routine outpatient visit. She reports feeling generally well with steady energy. Diet includes frequent sugary drinks and snacks between meals, which was discussed. She works as a nurse on rotating shifts and finds it hard to eat regularly. Mother with rheumatoid arthritis. Sleep is variable with her schedule; appetite is good. She has no new concerns today and is interested in preventive care. Lives with her partner. Never smoker, occasional alcohol.

O:
BP 116/72, HR 72, RR 14, Temp 98.1 F, SpO2 99% on room air. Weight 150 lb, BMI 24.
General: well appearing, in no distress.
HEENT: normal.
Neck: no lymphadenopathy, no thyromegaly.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: soft, nontender.
Extremities: no edema, joints without swelling.
Labs (prior week): A1c 6.0%, fasting glucose 102 mg/dL, lipid panel within goal, basic metabolic panel normal.

A/P:
1. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Reviewed reducing sugary drinks, planning balanced snacks around shifts, and adding regular walks on days off. Recheck A1c in 6 months and set a goal of modest weight loss.
2. Family history: reviewed relevant family history with patient and discussed age-appropriate screening and reassurance.
3. Health maintenance: cervical screening up to date; mammography discussed for the future. Influenza vaccine offered in the fall. Reviewed the recommended immunization schedule.
4. Lifestyle: discussed strategies for consistent meals and sleep while working rotating shifts, plus hydration and stress management.

Return in 6 months to review A1c, sooner as needed.
